The {{nihongo|'''Komatsu [[light armored vehicle]]''' ([[Japanese language|Japanese]]: 軽装甲機動車;|kei-sōkō-kidōsha}} is a Japanese military vehicle first produced in 2002. Currently used exclusively by the [[Japan Self-Defense Force]] (JSDF), it has seen use in the [[Iraq War]]. It is built by [[Komatsu Limited]]. Defense Systems Division in [[Komatsu, Ishikawa]], [[Japan]].<ref>{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110713164734/http://www.komatsu.com/CompanyInfo/profile/outline/production.html|url=http://www.komatsu.com/CompanyInfo/profile/outline/production.html|archive-date=2011-07-13|access-date=2012-10-25|title=Komatsu Production Page|publisher=Komatsu}}</ref> Komatsu's factory designation for the vehicle is '''KU50W'''.<ref name="Prototype">{{cite web|url=http://type61tank.la.coocan.jp/lav-prototype.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304025950/http://type61tank.la.coocan.jp/lav-prototype.htm |title=Komatsu LAV Prototype |access-date=2012-10-25 |language=ja |archive-date=2016-03-04 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

The exterior resembles the [[Véhicule Blindé Léger|Panhard VBL]] used by the French army, but the LAV has 4 doors and a large cabin for carrying soldiers. The LAV can also be transported by air in vehicles like the CH-47J and the C-130H.<ref name="Mount">{{cite web|url=http://rightwing.sakura.ne.jp/equipment/jgsdf/vehicle/lamv/lamv.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121219093550/http://rightwing.sakura.ne.jp/equipment/jgsdf/vehicle/lamv/lamv.html |script-title=ja:軽装甲機動車 |access-date=2012-10-25 |language=ja |archive-date=2012-12-19 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==History==
[[File:P1060634 R 国際平和協力活動等（及び防衛協力等） 18.jpg|thumb|left|A Komatsu LAV with [[Japanese Iraq Reconstruction and Support Group]] markings in Samawa.]]
[[File:JGSDF Komatsu LAV.jpg|thumb|left|Komatsu LAV during demonstration in Yokosuka 2017]]

The Komatsu LAV was developed in 1997 to meet a [[Japan Ground Self-Defense Force|JGSDF]] need for an armored wheeled vehicle that could provide armored protection since their [[Toyota High Mobility Vehicle]]s and [[Mitsubishi Type 73 light truck]]s were not adequate to provide protection from small arms fire.<ref name="LAV"/> They were initially created with the concept of a potential Soviet invasion during the Cold War before they were relegated to anti-terrorist/invasion operations.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.defencereviewasia.com/articles/196/Protected-mobility-VEHICLES-SLOW-TO-ACCELERATE-IN-ASIA |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130614023042/http://www.defencereviewasia.com/articles/196/Protected-mobility-VEHICLES-SLOW-TO-ACCELERATE-IN-ASIA |title=Protected mobility- VEHICLES SLOW TO ACCELERATE IN ASIA |date=2012-12-20 |access-date=2013-06-14 |archive-date=2013-06-14 |publisher=Defence Review Asia |url-status=dead }}</ref>

It had made its first appearance in [[Kuwait]] when [[Japan Ground Self-Defense Force|JGSDF]] units had deployed the Komatsu LAV prior to humanitarian operations in [[Samawah]], a city in Iraq, 280&nbsp;km (174&nbsp;mi) southeast of Baghdad.<ref name="Blog">{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071202095224/http://blog.wired.com/defense/2007/03/five_for_fighti_7.html|url=http://blog.wired.com/defense/2007/03/five_for_fighti_7.html|title= Japan's slick armored vehicle|access-date=2013-06-14|archive-date=2007-12-02 |date=2007-03-19|author=Noah Shachtman}}</ref><ref name="Page">{{cite web|url=http://uroneko02.com/jgsdf_wepon01.htm |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130614125325/http://uroneko02.com/jgsdf_wepon01.htm |script-title=ja:軽装甲機動車 |language=ja |access-date=2013-06-14 |archive-date=2013-06-14 |url-status=dead }}</ref> An initial 400 LAVs were brought into JGSDF service in March 2005.<ref name="Blog"/> JASDF base security units are also equipped with the LAV as a main vehicle for patrols.<ref>{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081022205408/http://www15.tok2.com/home/lttom/military-powers_jasdf/omomezu/omomezu005.htm|url=http://www15.tok2.com/home/lttom/military-powers_jasdf/omomezu/omomezu005.htm|script-title=ja:ミリパワ的おもめず航空自衛隊 基地警備部隊車両編|access-date=2013-06-15|archive-date=2008-10-22 |language=ja}}</ref>

In February 2019, Komatsu formally announced it will no longer develop new models of the LAV, citing high cost in developing a new model and low profit return when production was first halted in 2017.<ref>{{Cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190222185554/https://www.janes.com/article/86737/komatsu-to-stop-developing-lav-for-jgsdf|archive-date=2019-02-22|url=https://www.janes.com/article/86737/komatsu-to-stop-developing-lav-for-jgsdf|title=Komatsu to stop developing LAV for JGSDF|last=Takahashi|first=Kosuke|date=21 February 2019|website=Jane's 360|access-date=8 March 2019}}</ref> They would only continue production for NBC recon vehicles.<ref>https://web.archive.org/web/20201007012244/https://euro-sd.com/2019/05/articles/13183/komatsus-withdrawal-from-the-armoured-vehicles-business/</ref>

==Variants==
No variants are known to be available, but the vehicle appears to have been built in at least three production models, namely '''KU50W-0002K''', '''KU50W-0003K''' and '''KU50W-0005K'''.<ref name="Prototype"/>

==Design==
[[File:13 01 018 R 自衛隊記念日 観閲式(Parade of Self-Defense Force) 30.jpg|right|thumb|Komatsu LAVs used by the JGSDF in a military parade. Note the split-type roof hatches and the machine gun shield.]]

The Komatsu LAV has open-split roof hatch of the vehicle provides additional protection to the gunner from all directions, if it is locked in an upright position.<ref name="Profile"/> The vehicles deployed in Iraq are fitted with reinforced bulletproof windshields, wire cutters and an armoured tub around the gun mount for extra protection.<ref name="Profile"/>

According to reports, the vehicle is bulletproof against 5.56 and 7.62 bullets.<ref name="Profile"/> It is unknown whether other bullet calibers can easily penetrate the LAV or not.

For the LAV's engine, it is fitted with a liquid cooled 4-cycle diesel engine of 160&nbsp;hp. The power pack is mounted centre forward of the vehicle to distribute weight more evenly between the axles. The propulsion system provides a top speed of 100&nbsp;km/h, traveling more than 200 miles without refueling.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www15.tok2.com/home/lttom/military-powers_jgsdf/other/military-powers_lav.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131003001058/http://www15.tok2.com/home/lttom/military-powers_jgsdf/other/military-powers_lav.html |title=軽装甲機動車 略称：LAV愛称：ライトアーマー |language=ja |access-date=2012-10-25 |archive-date=2013-10-03 |url-status=dead }}</ref> It is fitted with all run-flat tires. The low turning radius allows the vehicle to negotiate narrow passages.

The Komatsu LAV can be armed with the [[FN MINIMI|Sumitomo M249 LMG]] or [[M2 Browning machine gun|Sumitomo M2HB]] 12.7mm machine gun for anti-personnel duties.<ref name="Mount"/> It can also mount the [[Type 01 LMAT]] or a [[Type 87 Chu-MAT|Kawasaki Type 87 anti-tank missile]] for anti-armored missions. [[Smoke grenade]] dischargers can be mounted on the rear sides of the vehicle.<ref name="Mount"/>
